sentences: Your agent says: fixed, all tests pass.
But what if the suite passed before the fix, too?
Here's a real run.
The agent adds a test, and everything goes green.
RedGreen runs the same command again, on the pre-change tree.
Still green. The test proves nothing, so the claim is stamped unproven.
So the agent takes a shortcut.
It rewrites its old assertions to assert True.
The assertion count never moves, so a text counter misses it.
RedGreen reads the syntax tree, finds two assertions weakened to constants, and stamps it tampered.
Now the honest version.
A real regression test.
Without the fix, it fails. With the fix, it passes.
Red before, green after. That's proof.
Inside Hermes, the same engine runs as a plugin.
The pre-verify hook vetoes the claim, and once it is proven, the reply carries a proof badge.
Every proof is a certificate with a double-entry ledger.
Every changed file is a debit, and only a proven negative control settles it.
It even exports a share card.
RedGreen.
On fifty synthetic scenarios, the AST guard caught thirty of thirty tampering attempts, with no false alarms. A text counter caught twenty.
Zero dependencies. Runs locally, no API key.
